title: Drinking water total coliform (RTCR) practice questions
description: Free total coliform (RTCR) practice questions on 40 CFR 141 Subpart Y. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.topic: General provisions and laboratory methods
questions.question: What does 141.852(a)(2) require systems to determine about total coliforms and E. coli in a sample?

options.A: Only their presence or absence; a determination of density is not required
options.B: The most probable number per liter
options.C: The density in colonies per 100 ml
options.D: The density of E. coli only

questions.explanation: "Systems need only determine the presence or absence of total coliforms and E. coli; a determination of density is not required."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.852, Analytical methods and laboratory certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: General provisions and laboratory methods
questions.question: Footnote 4 to the method table in 141.852(a)(5) says exposure of filtration equipment to UV light is not adequate to ensure sterilization. Unless pre-sterilized disposable funnel units are used, how must every membrane filtration series begin?

options.A: With equipment rinsed in sodium thiosulfate
options.B: With equipment exposed to UV light for at least 2 minutes
options.C: With membrane filtration equipment that has been sterilized by autoclaving
options.D: With equipment wiped down with chlorine bleach

questions.explanation: "All filtration series must begin with membrane filtration equipment that has been sterilized by autoclaving. Exposure of filtration equipment to UV light is not adequate to ensure sterilization." UV may be used afterward only "to sanitize the funnels between filtrations within a filtration series."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.852, Analytical methods and laboratory certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Sample siting plans and sample validity
questions.question: Under 141.853(a)(2), which systems may collect all required total coliform samples on a single day, if the samples are taken from different sites?

options.A: Any community water system serving 10,000 or fewer people
options.B: Systems that use only ground water and serve 4,900 or fewer people
options.C: Systems serving more than 4,900 people that use surface water
options.D: Subpart H systems serving 1,000 or fewer people

questions.explanation: Samples go at regular intervals through the month, "except that systems that use only ground water and serve 4,900 or fewer people may collect all required samples on a single day if they are taken from different sites."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.853, General monitoring requirements for all public water systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Sample siting plans and sample validity
questions.question: A system takes special purpose samples to check whether disinfection was sufficient after a main repair. How does 141.853(b) treat those samples?

options.A: They must be included when calculating whether the coliform treatment technique trigger has been exceeded
options.B: They must not be used to determine whether the coliform treatment technique trigger has been exceeded
options.C: They count as repeat samples under 141.858
options.D: They count toward the trigger only if they are total coliform-positive

questions.explanation: Special purpose samples, "such as those taken to determine whether disinfection practices are sufficient following pipe placement, replacement, or repair, must not be used to determine whether the coliform treatment technique trigger has been exceeded."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.853, General monitoring requirements for all public water systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Sample siting plans and sample validity
questions.question: Under 141.853(c)(1)(i), what may the laboratory establish that allows the State to invalidate a total coliform-positive sample?

options.A: That all repeat samples are total coliform-negative
options.B: That the system has only one service connection
options.C: That the sample was collected on a weekend
options.D: That improper sample analysis caused the total coliform-positive result

questions.explanation: The State may invalidate a total coliform-positive sample when "The laboratory establishes that improper sample analysis caused the total coliform-positive result." It "may not invalidate a total coliform-positive sample solely on the grounds that all repeat samples are total coliform-negative."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.853, General monitoring requirements for all public water systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Non-community ground water systems serving 1,000 or fewer
questions.question: What routine total coliform monitoring frequency does 141.854(b) set for a non-community water system serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water, when it is not a seasonal system and none of paragraphs (c) through (h) and (j) changes its schedule?

options.A: Once every three years
options.B: Each week that the system provides water to the public
options.C: Each calendar quarter that the system provides water to the public
options.D: Twice a month

questions.explanation: "Systems must monitor each calendar quarter that the system provides water to the public, except for seasonal systems or as provided under paragraphs (c) through (h) and (j) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.854, Routine monitoring requirements for non-community water systems serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Non-community ground water systems serving 1,000 or fewer
questions.question: A non-community ground water system serving 1,000 or fewer people is on annual monitoring and has one subpart Y monitoring violation, with no other listed event. What does 141.854(f) require?

options.A: Begin quarterly monitoring the quarter following the event
options.B: Stop serving water until a Level 2 assessment is completed
options.C: Take one make-up sample and remain on annual monitoring
options.D: Begin weekly monitoring the week following the event

questions.explanation: Under 141.854(f), "A system on annual monitoring that experiences the event identified in paragraphs (f)(5) of this section must begin quarterly monitoring the quarter following the event"; (f)(5) is "one subpart Y monitoring violation for a system on annual monitoring."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.854, Routine monitoring requirements for non-community water systems serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Community ground water systems serving 1,000 or fewer
questions.question: A community water system serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water is on reduced (quarterly) monitoring and loses its certified operator. What does 141.855(d)(1) require?

options.A: Return to monthly monitoring after a rolling 12-month period
options.B: Complete a Level 2 assessment within 30 days
options.C: Stay on quarterly monitoring until the next sanitary survey
options.D: Return to monthly monitoring the month following that loss

questions.explanation: "A system that loses its certified operator must return to monthly monitoring the month following that loss."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.855, Routine monitoring requirements for community water systems serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Community ground water systems serving 1,000 or fewer
questions.question: What floor does 141.855(d)(1) set when the State reduces the monitoring frequency of a community water system serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water?

options.A: No less than once every six years
options.B: No less than annual monitoring
options.C: No less than once every three years
options.D: No less than quarterly monitoring

questions.explanation: "The State may reduce the monitoring frequency from monthly monitoring to no less than quarterly monitoring" if the system meets the listed criteria.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.855, Routine monitoring requirements for community water systems serving 1,000 or fewer people using only ground water (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Subpart H systems and systems serving more than 1,000
questions.question: Under 141.856(b), what routine total coliform monitoring frequency applies to a subpart H system serving 1,000 or fewer people, including a consecutive system?

options.A: Monthly, with no reduction allowed
options.B: Annually, after a State site visit equivalent to a Level 2 assessment
options.C: Quarterly, if it is in compliance with State-certified operator provisions
options.D: Quarterly, once it has a clean compliance history for 12 months

questions.explanation: "Subpart H systems of this part (including consecutive systems) must monitor monthly. Systems may not reduce monitoring."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.856, Routine monitoring requirements for subpart H public water systems serving 1,000 or fewer people (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Subpart H systems and systems serving more than 1,000
questions.question: Under 141.857(c), what must a subpart H system serving more than 1,000 people that does not practice filtration in compliance with subparts H, P, T and W do on each day its source water turbidity (measured as specified in 141.74(b)(2)) exceeds 1 NTU?

options.A: Collect three repeat samples at the entry point to the distribution system
options.B: Double the number of routine samples for that month
options.C: Collect at least one total coliform sample near the first service connection
options.D: Collect a coliform sample at the farthest point of the distribution system

questions.explanation: The system "must collect at least one total coliform sample near the first service connection each day the turbidity level of the source water, measured as specified in § 141.74(b)(2), exceeds 1 NTU."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.857, Routine monitoring requirements for public water systems serving more than 1,000 people (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Subpart H systems and systems serving more than 1,000
questions.question: 141.857(d) says systems serving more than 1,000 people may not reduce monitoring, with one exception. Which systems does that exception cover?

options.A: Subpart H community water systems serving fewer than 3,300 people
options.B: Non-community water systems using only ground water (not GWUDI) that serve 1,000 or fewer people in some months and more than 1,000 in other months
options.C: Any community water system using only ground water
options.D: Consecutive systems that buy all of their water from a wholesale system

questions.explanation: "Systems may not reduce monitoring, except for non-community water systems using only ground water (and not ground water under the direct influence of surface water) serving 1,000 or fewer people in some months and more than 1,000 persons in other months."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.857, Routine monitoring requirements for public water systems serving more than 1,000 people (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Repeat monitoring and E. coli testing
questions.question: Under 141.858(a)(2), repeat samples are normally collected on the same day. What may the State allow a system with a single service connection to do instead?

options.A: Collect the set over a three-day period, or collect a larger volume repeat sample(s) totaling at least 300 ml
options.B: Skip repeat sampling if next month's routine sample is negative
options.C: Collect a single 100 ml repeat sample
options.D: Collect the set at any time within 30 days

questions.explanation: "The State may allow a system with a single service connection to collect the required set of repeat samples over a three-day period or to collect a larger volume repeat sample(s) in one or more sample containers of any size, as long as the total volume collected is at least 300 ml." The State "cannot waive the requirement for a system to collect repeat samples".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.858, Repeat monitoring and E. coli requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Repeat monitoring and E. coli testing
questions.question: A system collects a routine sample and, before it learns the result, collects another routine sample from within five adjacent service connections. The first sample is then found to contain total coliforms. What does 141.858(a)(4) allow?

options.A: The system may count the second sample as a repeat sample instead of as a routine sample
options.B: The State must invalidate the first sample
options.C: The second sample becomes a special purpose sample
options.D: The system must discard the second sample

questions.explanation: If the system "collects another routine sample(s) from within five adjacent service connections of the initial sample, and the initial sample, after analysis, is found to contain total coliforms, then the system may count the subsequent sample(s) as a repeat sample instead of as a routine sample."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.858, Repeat monitoring and E. coli requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Repeat monitoring and E. coli testing
questions.question: Under 141.858(b)(2), on what basis may the State allow a system, case by case, to forgo E. coli testing on a total coliform-positive sample?

options.A: All repeat samples are total coliform-negative
options.B: The system serves fewer than 25 people
options.C: The system assumes that the total coliform-positive sample is E. coli-positive
options.D: The sample was collected at the end of the distribution system

questions.explanation: The State may allow a system "to forgo E. coli testing on a total coliform-positive sample if that system assumes that the total coliform-positive sample is E. coli-positive." The system must then notify the State as in (b)(1), and "the provisions of § 141.63(c) apply."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.858, Repeat monitoring and E. coli requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Treatment technique triggers and assessments
questions.question: Which item does 141.859(b)(2) list among the minimum elements the assessor must review when conducting a Level 1 or Level 2 assessment?

options.A: The system's water rates and billing records
options.B: The operators' certification exam scores
options.C: Sample sites, sampling protocol and sample processing
options.D: The system's public notification history under subpart Q

questions.explanation: The assessor evaluates "minimum elements that include review and identification of inadequacies in sample sites; sampling protocol; sample processing", along with atypical events, distribution system changes, source and treatment considerations and "existing water quality monitoring data."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.859, Coliform treatment technique triggers and assessment requirements for protection against potential fecal contamination (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Treatment technique triggers and assessments
questions.question: For a system with approved annual monitoring, which pattern does 141.859(a)(2) list as a Level 2 treatment technique trigger?

options.A: Submitting a monthly monitoring report late
options.B: One total coliform-positive sample in a year
options.C: One missed annual routine sample
options.D: A Level 1 trigger in two consecutive years

questions.explanation: Level 2 triggers include, "For systems with approved annual monitoring, a Level 1 trigger in two consecutive years."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.859, Coliform treatment technique triggers and assessment requirements for protection against potential fecal contamination (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Treatment technique triggers and assessments
questions.question: A completed assessment found sanitary defects that were not all corrected by the time the form was submitted. What does 141.859(c) require for the remaining corrections?

options.A: Complete them within 24 hours of submitting the form
options.B: Complete them on a timetable approved by the State in consultation with the system, and notify the State when each scheduled corrective action is completed
options.C: Nothing further, because submitting the form ends the system's duties
options.D: Repeat the full assessment every month until all defects are corrected

questions.explanation: "For corrections not completed by the time of submission of the assessment form, the system must complete the corrective action(s) in compliance with a timetable approved by the State in consultation with the system. The system must notify the State when each scheduled corrective action is completed."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.859, Coliform treatment technique triggers and assessment requirements for protection against potential fecal contamination (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Violations, reporting and recordkeeping
questions.question: Which situation does 141.860(a) list as a violation of the MCL for E. coli?

options.A: The system has one total coliform-positive routine sample in which E. coli are not present
options.B: The system fails to take every required routine sample in a compliance period
options.C: The system fails to submit a completed assessment form after properly conducting the assessment
options.D: The system fails to take all required repeat samples following an E. coli-positive routine sample

questions.explanation: 141.860(a)(3): "The system fails to take all required repeat samples following an E. coli-positive routine sample." Missing routine samples is a monitoring violation and a late assessment form is a reporting violation.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.860, Violations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Violations, reporting and recordkeeping
questions.question: What deadline does 141.861(a)(4) set for a system to report a coliform monitoring violation to the State?

options.A: By the end of the day the system discovers the violation
options.B: Within 10 days after the system discovers the violation
options.C: Within 48 hours after the system discovers the violation
options.D: Within 90 days after the system discovers the violation

questions.explanation: A system that failed a coliform monitoring requirement "must report the monitoring violation to the State within 10 days after the system discovers the violation, and notify the public in accordance with subpart Q of this part."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.861, Reporting and recordkeeping (as of Nov 3, 2026)
